brief: A sewing-room tower: drawers on the ground storey, open bins on the top storey, at least two storeys.

requirements.evidence: Two storeys: level 0 (piece:0,0,0;half-n, piece:0,1,0;half-n) + level 1 (piece:0,0,1;half-n, piece:0,1,1;half-n).
Ground storey: drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:0#0,1#cut on the two half-n bases at level 0.
Top storey: bin:0,0,1 div2 and bin:0,1,1 open bins at level 1, dressed with standing marker/brush to show open storage.
requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey

finish.summary: Two-storey sewing-room tower: two drawers on the ground storey, two open bins on the top storey, capped and locked, dressed with sewing-room notions.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: A base goes beside a base on the same storey, or on top of one of the same kind. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now.
